subject: economics
title: Productivity Maths Mission
welcome_lead: A car plant boss needs you. Calculate output, unit costs and figure out whether new robots are worth the investment.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics calculations adventure on productivity, unit costs and capital vs labour intensive production.
final_note: Productivity calculations conquered. Stretch yourself in the exam-style finale!

walkthroughs.body_html: Productivity = output ÷ (workers × hours). A bakery bakes 600 loaves with 5 staff working 6 hours: 600 ÷ (5 × 6) = 20 loaves per worker per hour. If a new oven raises output to 900 loaves with the same staff/hours, productivity jumps to 30.

Unit cost = total cost ÷ output. Total cost £2,400, output 600 = £4 per unit. Same total cost, output 900 = £2.67. Higher productivity slashed unit cost by 33%. That's why firms invest in machines and training.

Car factories are capital intensive (robots dominate). Hairdressing is labour intensive. Choice depends on relative cost of labour vs capital, type of product and skills available. In the UK, rising wages push firms toward more automation.

options: When demand rises, the supply curve shifts right to meet it.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.

options: Revenue is profit before tax and profit is revenue after tax.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity); profit is what remains after deducting costs from revenue.
Revenue and profit mean the same thing.
